card.law_is_about: Civil and criminal protection against digital violence, including disclosure of account data.
card.they_want: Extend disclosure to telecom and email providers to identify authors.
card.they_claim: Even prepaid SIM purchase within the EU requires data verification.
card.the_problem: EU countries have different rules; Finnish anonymous prepaid services supply a counterexample.

claim_quote.original: Innerhalb der EU erfordert nämlich selbst die Anschaffung einer Prepaid-Karte die Verifikation von Daten
claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: Within the EU, even purchasing a prepaid card requires verification of data

request_quote.original: auf Telekommunikationsanbieter und E-Mailprovider verwertbar zu machen
request_quote.translation_en: Translation of request fragment: to make [the disclosure claim] usable against telecommunications and email providers
request_quote.note: Short exact fragment; the full sentence expressly recommends the extension.

counter_quote.original: The issue of access to prepaid SIM cards is not regulated at EU level.

supplementary_counter_quote.original: The number of an anonymous prepaid service can not be ported.

correction: There is no general EU requirement. The Presidency note distinguishes Member States that require identification from those allowing anonymous purchases. Finland’s regulator recognises anonymous prepaid service; a Finnish operator’s terms expressly permit service activation without authentication.
effect: Narrows the assumed coverage of verified telephone identities supporting the requested extension.
limits: The preceding sentence says telephone numbers often permit identification, which can remain true. The paragraph may generalise from German practice. This does not show German identification requirements are absent, disclosure is never useful, or the proposed extension is unwise.
materiality_explanation: Minor: the geographical generalisation overstates coverage, while domestic and many other numbers can still be identified. The broader policy case survives.
direction_explanation: The claim makes telephone disclosure look more reliably useful across the EU, supporting the author’s explicit extension request. No intent is inferred.
context_checked: Read all of section 2.3.a and adjacent sections 2.2 and 2.3.b. The disputed sentence is explicitly EU-wide; the paragraph does not restrict it to German TKG requirements.
The preceding statement uses a frequency qualification for identifying numbers; preserve this and do not turn it into a claim that every telephone user can always be identified.
The identification example mentions a document and Post-Ident, suggesting possible generalisation from German practice. This is an alternative explanation, not an intent finding.
